questions.stem: You are working on a cell line derived from a malignant colonic tumor. During the observation of your cells using the laboratory light microscope, you notice an intense bright spot at the center of the field of view, with a progressive decrease in light intensity toward the periphery. Which component should be adjusted to correct this finding?
options: tube connecting the objectives to the eyepieces.

questions.stem: In this cell line, you intend to analyze the distribution of mitochondria. You choose to use fluorochromes. Which fluorochrome is the most appropriate for this experiment?
After fluorescent labeling (rhodamine), you examine the slides using a fluorescence microscope. At which wavelength should the excitation filter be set to visualize mitochondria?
What is the emission wavelength of the used fluorochrome (rhodamine)?
The next step of your project consists of isolating mitochondria by cell fractionation. You begin with the homogenization of your sample. Which conditions must be respected to preserve mitochondria?
After homogenization, which protocol should be followed to isolate a large quantity of mitochondria from your sample?
options: differential ultracentrifugation followed by density gradient ultracentrifugation.
density gradient ultracentrifugation followed by differential ultracentrifugation.

questions.stem: After isolation of mitochondria, you aim to study the precise organization of transporters within the inner mitochondrial membrane. Which technique is the most appropriate for this study?
To move forward, a migrating cell forms a lamellipodium. Which cytoskeletal event is directly responsible for this extension?
options: the depolymerization of actin filaments at the front of the cell.
the polymerization of actin, pushing the membrane forward.

questions.stem: A drug that prevents tubulin polymerization will result in:
options: disruption of mitotic spindle formation during cell division.

questions.stem: Intermediate filaments are directly involved in:
The centrosome plays a key role in cytoskeleton organization. Among the following statements, which are correct?
options: it constitutes the main microtubule-organizing center (MTOC).
it orients the growth of microtubules formed from gamma and beta tubulin.
it directly regulates the polymerization of actin filaments.
it participates in organizing the mitotic spindle during cell division.

options: differs from both bacterial and eukaryotic rRNA.

questions.stem: Concerning exocytosis:
options: regulated exocytosis requires an external signal (hormone/neurotransmitter) and occurs in specialized secretory cells.
constitutive exocytosis transports vesicles from the trans-Golgi network (TGN) to the plasma membrane.

questions.stem: In Na⁺/glucose symport in enterocytes:
options: 2 Na⁺ + 1 glucose enter through SGLT1 at the apical membrane.
glucose exits through GLUT2 at the basal membrane.
Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase maintains the Na⁺ gradient by extruding Na⁺.
glucose enters by simple diffusion at the apical surface.

questions.stem: Specializations of the cell periphery:
options: cilia and flagella are important for cell motility or movement of surrounding fluids.
microvilli function mainly to increase surface area for absorption and exchange.
cilia and flagella are important for membrane glycosylation.

questions.stem: Caveolae are:
options: small flask-shaped invaginations derived from lipid rafts.

questions.stem: Compared with the plasma membrane, ER membrane lipids are characterized by:
options: longer aliphatic chains and higher cholesterol content.
shorter aliphatic chains and lower cholesterol content → increased fluidity.

options: passage through the translocon pore back to the cytosol.
assistance of an ER chaperone molecule.
